Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Larkin (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Echelon Head of Platform), Ivy Zhao (Echelon SRE Lead), Rahul Banerjee (Echelon CTO), Tara Kim (QA)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. uh, goal is to walk through the fallback reconciliation we promised, and nail down the runbook and the tighter SLO ask from Echelon.
[00:18] Carlos: thanks, Maya. quick context — we've had two customer-impacting blips in jan, both where the hosted endpoint fell back to the smaller quant model and that increased hallucinations for a subset of flows. customers flagged it so we had to roll back.
[00:35] Ivy: yeah and from our side the problem looked like the kv cash — the cache — sorry, the KV cache got evicted then the prefix-miss caused a higher token count; latency spiked and the fallback to the cheaper variant happened.
[00:50] Jon: okay that tracks. on our side the policy was configured to fallback when 95th p99 latency exceeded 700ms, but i remember the burst policy had a short window that could cascade.
[01:05] Rahul: just to be clear, we want to tighten our SLA from 99.9 to 99.95 but we're worried about cost. so this session is to figure out mitigations that give us that reliability without 3x spend.
[01:20] Maya: yep. we believe a combination of prefix caching, small model warming, and an adjusted fallback cooldown can reduce the cascade without a big cost hit. we'll walk through the proposed runbook and a couple test plans.
[01:37] Tara: also QA found a regression where the fallback didn't preserve structured output schema in the smaller variant; transcripts showed missing fields. not sure if that's Redwood model mismatch or our validation.
[01:50] Priya: good catch. we'll include schema-preservation as a validation step in the runbook.
[02:05] Ivy: quick note — our infra team observed that the autoscaler for the dedicated pool (we're on a semi-dedicated config) sometimes delayed new instances by 25s. that delay lines up with the KV cache refresh window.
[02:22] Jon: hmm, the autoscale latency combined with the batch build-up could definitely push the p99. we should capture that metric in the test.
[02:36] Carlos: can we get a timeline from Redwood for a permanent fix vs interim mitigations? we need that for our execs.
[02:45] Maya: yes. interim — runbook + config tweaks — we can deliver in ~5 business days. permanent — runtime changes to reduce eviction likelihood and smarter async pre-warming — that's a 6-8 week roadmap item.
[03:02] Rahul: okay 6-8 weeks is acceptable if mitigations land first. we will need clear rollback steps and a live test.
[03:12] Maya: got it. i'll go through the runbook detail now.
[03:18] Maya: Step 1: detection — ensure p95/p99 and KV cache miss rate alerts are wired to your pager; runbook will include thresholds and synthetic checks. we recommend a 10s synthetic ping for hot routes and a 30s synthetic for background.
[03:36] Ivy: we already have synthetic pings but not for the hot conversational routes; we'll add them.
[03:42] Maya: Step 2: controlled throttling — during spikes, rather than instantaneous fallback to the small quant-variant, we suggest a staged fallback: first degrade beam-size / max-tokens, then route a small % of traffic to the smaller variant for a measured canary.
[03:58] Jon: important nuance — the smaller variant in your configuration doesn't include the schema post-processing hook by default; that explains tara's issue. recommend to enable the post-process hook on all model variants.
[04:13] Tara: yes please, that would likely fix our missing-fields problem.
[04:18] Maya: Step 3: KV cache warming — when a new instance spins up, prefetch the top-k prefixes based on recent traffic; Redwood can supply a small warm-up lambda that hits the instance with top prefixes to populate cache. this avoids the first-request penalty.
[04:33] Carlos: is that safe for PIi? some prefixes contain user tokens.
[04:38] Priya: we suggest sampling non-sensitive prefixes or using synthetic prompts derived from your anonymized logs. we'll put a template.
[04:46] Ivy: any network egress concerns on warmup? we have strict egress policies.
[04:50] Jon: warmup is internal to the VPC if you're on private; for hosted it's over our encrypted link. we can also bundle the prefixes into a container image for on-prem to avoid extra traffic.
[05:05] Maya: Step 4: fallback cooldown and hysteresis — extend cooldown windows and require sustained elevated p99 for 2 consecutive intervals before a hard fallback. reduces flip-flopping.
[05:18] Carlos: ok but does that risk higher latencies for some requests?
[05:22] Jon: there is a small tradeoff; that's why staged fallback and dynamic throttling are important — we want to avoid the sharp switch that causes hallucination regressions.
[05:33] Rahul: can you quantify the cost delta for these changes? rough ballpark is fine.
[05:37] Maya: quick estimate — with prefix caching and staged fallback we expect <15% increase versus current; with rigid 99.95 SLO and more reserved capacity it could go up to ~30-40%. we'll give a spreadsheet with scenario rows.
[05:52] Maya: moving on, i'll open the shared doc — link: https://redwood.internal/docs/ec-fallback-runbook (note: internal link).
[06:00] Ivy: i can't open that from my laptop, it's blocked; can you share a viewable copy?
[06:05] Maya: sure, we'll publish a customer copy to the Echelon drive, i'll attach after the call.
[06:10] [06:10] (background noise / crosstalk)
[06:30] Carlos: i'd like to walk the Jan 28th trace with you — we captured a wall clock from our router showing a burst of request retries.
[06:40] Jon: great, can you drop a trace link in the doc? that will help us correlate.
[06:46] Carlos: yes will do.
[06:48] [07:00] Maya: okay checklist for the interim patch: 1) enable post-process hook on small variant, 2) change fallback policy to staged w/ canary %, 3) add prefix warmup on instance boot, 4) increase cooldown to 2 intervals. should we prioritize 1 and 2?
[07:15] Ivy: 1 and 2 are highest priority for us, then 3. 4 is less urgent but helpful.
[07:23] Rahul: agree.
[07:28] Tara: we also want a unit test that asserts schema preservation across variants — can we get a small harness?
[07:34] Jon: yes we can provide a test harness repo and some sample prompts.
[07:38] Maya: good.
[07:40] [08:00] Priya: quick ops note — we'll add a runbook section for customer comms template so you can notify users pre/post test.
[08:10] Carlos: thanks.
[08:15] Maya: now for the live failover test — proposed approach: run a controlled chaos test that simulates an instance eviction (or simulating high queue time) and watch whether staged fallback + warmup prevents heavy regression. we recommend a canary at 2% then 10% traffic.
[08:34] Ivy: what metrics should we watch? p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, hallucination rate (per your eval harness), and schema-failure count.
[08:45] Jon: yes and also token-cost-per-request so we can estimate spend.
[08:50] Carlos: we will need a go/no-go checklist to pause the test if customer errors exceed threshold.
[08:56] Maya: absolutely — we'll include thresholds in the test plan.
[09:05] Rahul: one more constraint — our compliance team requires audit logs for any warmup or synthetic prompts hitting customer data. can you ensure logs are flagged as synthetic?
[09:18] Priya: yes, we can add a synthetic flag and ensure it's excluded from retention policies and PIi stores.
[09:27] Tara: FYI our QA will also run the harness against a 1% production snapshot earlier next week.
[09:34] Maya: great. we'll sync on scheduling.
[09:38] [10:00] Jon: i'd like to call out an underlying runtime fix that would help long-term — smarter KV eviction heuristics that keep frequently accessed prefixes sticky across scale events. this needs kernel-level heuristics and that's the 6-8 week item.
[10:18] Ivy: understandable. can we get visibility into the prioritization? we'd like to know if that moves up.
[10:24] Maya: i'll bring it to product and engineering prioritization; we can move it earlier if the test shows continued regressions.
[10:33] Carlos: what's the rollback plan if something in the staged fallback increases customer-visible errors?
[10:40] Jon: rollback is immediate — disable staged flag and reinstate previous policy. runbook will include exact CLI/API call examples.
[10:48] Maya: i'll ensure the runbook has the API snippets.
[10:51] [11:00] Carlos: about observability — we need per-route token breakdown tied to request ids. currently our traces show aggregate token counts only.
[11:09] Priya: Redwood console can provide token-level traces with request-id tagging; i'll request a sample export for you.
[11:17] Ivy: also add KV hit/miss per request if possible.
[11:20] Jon: yep, we'll push a telemetry delta to show KV hit rate.
[11:25] [12:00] Tara: one more QA note — some of our nightly regression jobs mask transient fallback; can we schedule a regression suite that includes fallback scenarios so we catch it earlier?
[12:37] Priya: we can provide a small regression bundle you can run in CI.
[12:42] Carlos: perfect.
[12:47] [13:00] Rahul: i want to talk briefly about contract language — tightened SLA means different remedies; we will need a clause that accounts for degraded quality from fallback decisions.
[13:13] Maya: our legal team has a standard SLO amendment template; we'll share and we can map the mitigation steps as credits or remediation.
[13:23] Rahul: thanks.
[13:27] [14:00] Maya: ok i want to surface a small caveat — staged fallback increases complexity of debugging because multiple variants might be active; we must ensure traces clearly indicate which variant served the response. we'll add a variant-id header.
[14:40] Ivy: agreed. that will help debugging.
[14:46] [15:00] Carlos: timeline recap?
[15:04] Maya: interim runbook + config changes — deliver by 2027-02-24; test bench and dedicated test capacity by 2027-02-22; live failover test targeted for week of 2027-02-28; permanent runtime fix estimate 6-8 weeks.
[15:25] Carlos: ok.
[15:28] [16:00] Tara: can we get a short deck for execs that summarizes impact, cost delta and go/no-go?
[16:09] Maya: yes we'll produce a 1-pager and a short slide deck.
[16:14] Priya: i'll own the 1-pager.
[16:18] [17:00] Jon: i'll attach the KV heatmap and a couple sample traces to the doc.
[17:12] Carlos: i'll send the Jan 28th trace and the router logs.
[17:18] [18:00] (brief pause)
[18:15] Rahul: any blocker from Redwood side to run the failover test?
[18:22] Jon: none from infra, we just need the test window and sampling policy; provisioning test capacity might take a few hours to spin but we'll do it ahead.
[18:33] Maya: ok to confirm next steps on the call: Priya to post runbook draft, Jon to share heatmap and harness, Maya to share pricing scenarios and API snippets, Carlos to share traces. schedule the live test next week.
[18:51] Ivy: sounds good.
[18:55] Carlos: thanks everyone.
[19:00] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the doc and action items.
